t.E472d.agn: In 2020 EFSA set an ADI based on the group ADI of 240 mg/kg body weight, expressed as tartaric acid, and found no safety concern at the reported use levels. In its 2025 follow-up opinion EFSA cited an ADI of 480 mg/kg body weight for this additive and stated that estimated intake remained below this value.
t.E472d.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acid (tartaric acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472d.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472d.prod: It is an emulsifier obtained by esterification of mono- and diglycerides with tartaric acid; according to the 2020 EFSA evaluation, the production method is not described in the sources and there is no manufacturer on the market.
t.E472d.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI set based on the tartaric acid group ADI (240 mg/kg body weight per day), no safety concern.
t.E472d.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: ADI of 480 mg/kg body weight per day; estimated intake below the ADI. Insufficient technical data submitted for a change to the specifications.
t.E472d.summary: An emulsifier derived from mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It improves texture in bread, cake and margarine; the fat source may be vegetable or animal.
t.E472d.what: As an emulsifier, it strengthens the structure of dough.
